items.originalTitle: Decision time looms for Colton Herta after 2027 Cadillac F1 snub
detailZh: 决定时刻临近，科尔顿·赫塔在2027年凯迪拉克F1的拒绝后面临一个关键的职业抉择
随着他进入一级方程式的努力遭遇阻碍，科尔顿·赫塔现在面临一个关键的职业决定
凯迪拉克决定继续与经验丰富的老将瓦尔特里·博塔斯搭档塞吉奥·佩雷斯，这是在2026年一级方程式第11支车队首秀赛季问题缠身之后，为了连续性和稳定性做出的选择。这也引发了关于科尔顿·赫塔下一步将何去何从的关键问题
随着凯迪拉克的大多数股东TWG对不久的将来拥有一位美国车手驾驶其赛车的前景着迷，车队不惜一切代价将赫塔带到车队，让他离开了与其姐妹车队安德里蒂全球的舒适环境，为了现在或永不的机会去尝试进入一级方程式
Herta，一位九次赢得IndyCar赛事的车手，也是迄今为止最年轻的一位，面临着调整到欧洲赛车运动的挑战，包括掌握F2中特有的Pirelli轮胎，这些轮胎他也会在F1中遇到。
这与他进行的私人测试相辅相成——凯迪拉克没有之前的赛车，因此从阿尔派恩租了一辆进行测试——以及多次大奖赛FP1练习，以增加他的超级驾照积分达到关键的40分。
在巴西进行的今年第六次此类测试后，Herta终于达到了这个神奇数字。但就在那时，凯迪拉克首席执行官Dan Towriss和车队负责人Marcin Budkowski开始就保留博塔斯的想法达成一致，将Herta作为2027年的官方预备车手，准备在博塔斯无法在赛季前半段提升他的表现上限时介入。
凯迪拉克可能没有考虑到的是，Herta对被忽视的消息的反应。据悉，这位26岁的美国人在目前拒绝了预备车手的角色，并决定不完成他在Hitech的麻烦F2赛季，放弃了在卡塔尔和阿布扎比的最后两轮比赛。
瓦尔特里·博塔斯，凯迪拉克车队，塞尔吉奥·佩雷斯，凯迪拉克车队
虽然这个决定可能因为他对错过机会的最初失望而变得模糊，赫塔也渴望继续在竞争性比赛中驾驶，而不是坐在场边，但这个立场多少有些令人惊讶。在37岁的博塔斯之后成为凯迪拉克的第三车手，似乎在整个车队的整个 paddock 中，无论是2027年还是2028年，都是最有机会晋升F1的位置。
“我们给他提供了一个预备位置，”托里斯在拉斯维加斯说。“这个位置为’28年空着，所以Colton有选择。在其他运动中也有选择。我认为他已经决定了一个方向，但我们仍在讨论这个话题，并期待看到Colton想要做什么。”
“这绝对是一个艰难的决定，与Colton的艰难讨论。我认为他感到失望。为此投入了大量的工作，大量的准备工作[已经完成]。我知道Colton非常勇敢，甚至愿意承担这个风险，进入F2并尝试在短时间内吸收所有这些知识。”
这个角色被认为对于一名预备车手来说非常有利，而且当赛道扩展到33个参赛者时，它还可以与一次性的印第安纳波利斯500赛事相结合。
赫塔现在面临着一项决定自己职业生涯的重大决定，因为2028年的赌注很大。如果他能在测试中留下足够好的印象以取代博塔斯，那么这将是他在F1赛场上全职参赛的最早时间。鉴于预备车手们往往很快就会失去职业势头，这也可能是他最后一次这样做的机会。
与此同时，他的老东家也即将进行一次大规模的翻新。在超过16年后，印第安纳波利斯赛车将在2028年首次引入一款全新的赛车，Dallara IR-28，它在测试中获得了极高的评价，并配备了一台更强大的2.4升双涡轮增压V6引擎。
在这个愚蠢的季节的这个阶段，由于在印第安纳波利斯赛车中已经没有全职的机会，如果赫塔决定放弃他的F1梦想，那么他需要尽快重新定位自己，以便在2028赛季找到一席竞争之地，无论是TWG还是其他地方。在2028年回归，当新的底盘提供了一个全新的起点时，从竞争的角度来看，这将是最理想的时间。
无论如何，赫塔必须做出决定，因为2028年将是他成败的关键一年。要么他吞下自尊，给他的F1梦想最后一次机会，与凯迪拉克合作，要么他过早地放弃那个梦想，开始努力重返竞争激烈的印第安纳波利斯赛车座椅。
这个过程从他的下一步行动开始——就在这里，就在现在。
detailEn: Decision time looms for Colton Herta after 2027 Cadillac F1 snub
With his campaign to get to Formula 1 hitting a roadblock, Colton Herta now faces a crucial career decision

Cadillac's decision to stick with veteran incumbent Valtteri Bottas to partner Sergio Perez is a choice for continuity and stability after a debut campaign plagued with issues for Formula 1's 11th team in 2026. It also raises key questions over what's next for Colton Herta.

With Cadillac's majority owner TWG enamoured with the prospect of having an American driver in one of its cars before too long, the team spared no expense on bringing Herta over, leaving the comfort of his IndyCar seat with sister team Andretti Global for a now-or-never shot at making it to F1.

Herta, a nine-time IndyCar race winner and the youngest to ever do so, faced a tricky challenge of adjusting to European racing in Formula 2, including mastering the peculiar Pirelli tyres that he would also find in F1.

That was dovetailed with private testing - Cadillac has no previous cars, so it rented a test from Alpine - and a number of grand prix FP1 sessions to boost his number of superlicence points to the critical number of 40.

After his sixth such test of the year in Brazil, Herta finally got to the magic number. But around that time, Cadillac CEO Dan Towriss and team principal Marcin Budkowski started aligning on the idea of retaining Bottas, deploying Herta as the official reserve driver for 2027, ready to step in if Bottas couldn't raise his performance ceiling over the first part of the season.

What Cadillac perhaps wasn't factoring in, is how Herta took the news of being snubbed. It is understood that the 26-year-old American has turned down the reserve role for now and has also decided against finishing his troubled F2 campaign with Hitech, forfeiting the final two rounds in Qatar and Abu Dhabi.
Valtteri Bottas, Cadillac Racing, Sergio Perez, Cadillac Racing

While that decision may be clouded by his initial disappointment at missing out and Herta is desperate to keep racing competitively, rather than sit on the sidelines, it's a somewhat surprising position to hold. Being Cadillac's third driver behind 37-year-old Bottas still appears to be the position with the best odds of F1 promotion across the entire paddock, whether over the course of 2027 or in 2028.

"We've offered him a reserve position," Towriss said in Las Vegas. "The seat's open for ’28, so there are options on the table for Colton. There are options in other sports as well. I think he's decided on a direction, but we're still in conversations on that and look forward to seeing what Colton wants to do.

"It was definitely a tough decision, a tough discussion with Colton. I think he was disappointed. There was a lot of work, a lot of a build-up [that went] into this. I know Colton was very brave in even taking on this risk, going into F2 and trying to cram all this learning in."
The role, which is understood to be rather lucrative for a reserve driver, could also be paired with a one-off Indy 500 outing when the grid expands to 33 entries.

Herta is now facing a career defining decision because of what's at stake in 2028. That is now the earliest he can get onto the F1 grid full-time if he makes a good enough impression to replace Bottas. It is likely also the last opportunity to do so, given how quickly reserve drivers tend to lose career momentum.

At the same time, his old home is also due a major renovation. For the first time in over 16 years, IndyCar will introduce an all-new car in 2028, the Dallara IR-28 which debuted to rave reviews in testing and is armed with a beefier 2.4l twin-turbo V6 engine.

With no full-time opportunities in IndyCar left for 2027 at this stage of the silly season, if Herta is deciding to call time on his F1 dream, then he needs to reposition himself as soon as possible to land a competitive seat for IndyCar 2028's season, whether that be with TWG or elsewhere. Returning in 2028, when the new chassis offers a blank slate, would be the most desirable timing from a competitive standpoint.

In any case, Herta has a decision to make as 2028 will be his make-or-break year. Either he swallows his pride and gives his F1 dream one last shot with Cadillac, or he abandons that dream prematurely and starts working on returning to a competitive IndyCar seat.
That process starts with his next move - right here, right now.

items.originalTitle: The issue that cost Pierre Gasly a potential "win" at F1's Las Vegas GP
detailZh: 导致皮埃尔·加斯利在F1拉斯维加斯大奖赛上错失潜在胜利的问题
阿尔派车手加斯利最终排名第五，但在比赛过半时曾一度位列第三
安德烈亚·基米·安东内利、梅赛德斯、兰多·诺里斯、麦克拉伦、皮埃尔·加斯利、阿尔派
皮埃尔·加斯利认为，如果冷却问题没有在比赛最后阶段影响他的阿尔派一级方程式赛车，他本有可能赢得拉斯维加斯大奖赛。
法国人从第八位发车最终获得第五名，但在原定50圈中的第31圈后，加斯利排在第三位，仅次于红牛车队的最终获胜者维斯塔潘和梅赛德斯车队的乔治·拉塞尔。
然而，加斯利在接下来的四圈中突然失去了五个位置，从第八位降至兰多·诺里斯、奥斯卡·皮亚斯特里、基米·安东内利、刘易斯·汉密尔顿和查尔斯·勒克莱尔之后。
这位30岁的车手解释说，这是由于他的A526赛车出现技术问题，最终由于拉塞尔撞上护栏以及法拉利车队的汉密尔顿和勒克莱尔相撞，他最终获得第五名。
因此，当被问及是否对错过他职业生涯的第六个领奖台感到沮丧时，加斯利在周六晚上回应说：“我不会这么说。但我会从事实上开始，这是我们作为团队最好的比赛，我们肯定会吸取积极的方面。”
他的2026赛季最佳成绩是在上海的第二轮比赛中获得第六名，尽管他在结果在法庭上得到解决之前，暂时被授予了摩纳哥的领奖台。
“事实上，那是一场非常有趣的比赛，我很享受在车队前列的战斗，”加斯利补充道。“但然后，是的，在比赛开始时我们飞得很快，我设法一路冲到了P3的位置。
“在那个时刻，我真的觉得我们可能有足够的速度去挑战胜利。当我到达P3时，我通过无线电被告知赛车过热，我不得不降低功率。
“我们降低了45圈的功率。所以当我切换到最激进的开关来冷却赛车时，我一路跌到了5号弯。我在直道上失去了位置，所以在那一圈里我失去了两个位置，然后我就一路退到了后面。我们正在管理赛车的温度。
“我必须打开差距。我可以在变速箱里，但我必须打开差距来冷却汽车。我真的觉得我们有机会获得领奖台，我一直要求恢复全功率，但只被允许在最后两圈这样做。”
“我们将审查确切发生了什么，因为我看到你们所有人都穿着冬季夹克，我穿着一件冬季夹克。我真的不明白为什么汽车会过热，但除此之外，这是整个团队不可思议的努力。”
气温低至9摄氏度，这让加斯利对问题感到困惑，尽管他认为这可能会比他保持第10名所获得的第五名更糟糕。
“我认为我们没有预料到这一点，”他声称。“但是，是的，这些45圈，我认为在最极端的情况下，我每圈损失超过一秒，因为我们运行的是那个最慢的引擎模式。”
“我很高兴排在第五，但确实，赛车非常快，还有更多的潜力可以挖掘。在跑极端策略的时候，我损失了很多，我以为我会比现在退得更远。”
““我试图保持稳定，我们在中间尝试了四五种不同的模式。最极端的一次，我想我可能使用了大约10圈，这是比赛中最令人担忧的部分，因为有了拖车增益，我在跟随其他车辆并进行尾流超车。”"
““但正如我说的，我们会回顾。这是赛车的一部分，但我认为这确实让我们损失了很多。”"
detailEn: The issue that cost Pierre Gasly a potential "win" at F1's Las Vegas GP
The Alpine driver finished fifth but was as high as third over halfway through
Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes, Lando Norris, McLaren, Pierre Gasly, Alpine
Pierre Gasly reckons he potentially had the pace to win the Las Vegas Grand Prix, had a cooling issue not affected his Alpine Formula 1 car in the closing stages.
The Frenchman finished fifth from eighth on the grid, but after 31 of the scheduled 50 laps, Gasly was third behind Red Bull’s eventual winner Max Verstappen and Mercedes’ George Russell.
Yet Gasly suddenly lost five positions within the next four laps, having dropped into eighth behind Lando Norris, Oscar Piastri, Kimi Antonelli, Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc.

The 30-year-old explained that this was down to a technical issue on his A526, which eventually took fifth due to Russell hitting the barriers plus Ferrari duo Hamilton and Leclerc colliding into each other.

So when asked afterwards if he was frustrated to miss out on his sixth career podium, Gasly responded on Saturday night: “I'm not going to call it that way. But I'll start with the fact that it's our best race as a team, and we're definitely going to take the positives.”
His previous best result in the 2026 F1 season was sixth at round two in Shanghai, despite him temporarily being given a Monaco podium until that result was settled in the courts.

“Follow with the fact that it was a very fun race to be part of and I enjoyed a lot battling at the front of the pack,” added Gasly. “But then yeah, at the start we were flying, I managed to find my way all the way up to P3.

“At that point I really felt that we had the pace to maybe even challenge for the win. And the moment I got to P3, I got told on the radio that the car was overheating and I had to turn down the power.

“We turned down the power for 45 laps. So the moment I went to the most aggressive switch to cool it down, I lost position all the way to Turn 5. I lost the position on the back straight, so I lost two positions in a lap and then I just dropped back all the way. We were managing the temperature.

“I had to open the gap. I could be in the gearbox, but I had to open the gap to cool down the car. I really feel we had the podium, and I kept asking to get back to full power, but I was only allowed to do it for the last two laps.

“We'll review exactly what happened, because I can see you guys all wearing winter jackets, I am wearing a winter jacket. I don't really understand why the car was overheating, but apart from that it was an incredible effort from all the team.”
Conditions were as low as 9C which left Gasly perplexed by the issue, though he reckons it could have been much worse than the fifth he took that keeps him 10th in the standings.
“I don't think we saw it coming,” he claimed. “But yeah, these 45 laps, I think the most extreme I was losing over a second a lap with that slowest engine mode that we were running.

“I'm happy to be fifth, but yeah, definitely the car was very fast, and there was more to take. At some point when I was running that extreme one, I was losing so much that I thought I was going to drop back even further than that.

“I was trying to hold down and we had four or five different modes we were playing in between. The most extreme, I think I had it for maybe 10 laps, which were the most worrying part of the race, because with the tow gain, I was following other cars and drafting back.
“But yeah, as I said, we'll review. It's part of racing, but I think it definitely cost us quite a bit too.”

detailZh: F1评论员呼吁法拉利拿出真正的后果：“我会让奥利·贝尔曼顶替一场”
詹姆斯·欣奇克利夫建议，在拉斯维加斯大奖赛的冲突之后，法拉利应让奥利弗·贝尔曼顶替一位车手出战一场比赛
夏尔·勒克莱尔，法拉利，刘易斯·汉密尔顿，法拉利
致法拉利车迷。来自马拉内罗及更远地方的最新法拉利F1新闻、车手动态、技术分析和比赛反应。
在2026年拉斯维加斯大奖赛上，夏尔·勒克莱尔和刘易斯·汉密尔顿在三场比赛内第二次相撞后，围场内的讨论很快就不再是谁在7号弯判断失误，而是转向了一个更难的问题：法拉利究竟怎样才能真正阻止这种事再次发生？
前印地赛车手詹姆斯·欣奇克利夫在F1 TV赛后节目中表示，车队领队弗雷德·瓦塞尔或许需要拿出终极威慑手段——把正式车手席位交给法拉利青训车手奥利弗·贝尔曼。
“你接下来该怎么办？我的意思是，你不能把其中一人摁在替补席上——那才是你想做的，”欣奇克利夫开场说道，搭档评论员乔利恩·帕尔默插话道：“也许你可以。”
欣奇克利夫立刻顺着这个想法说下去。“我的意思是，我会把贝尔曼塞进去跑一场，让其中一人坐一场，然后说，‘让我们给你们俩上一课’，就像，这里会有严重的后果，”他说，“但我不知道弗雷德还能做什么，所以我同意你；我真的很替他难过。
在欣奇克利夫看来，第38圈的那次纠缠之所以令人费解，是因为它发生在一场创纪录的352次超车大战的背景之下。“这不是摩纳哥。那不是你唯一一次超车机会，所以不要冒不必要的风险，”他指出。
夏尔·勒克莱尔，法拉利；刘易斯·汉密尔顿，法拉利
尽管如此，欣奇克利夫对赛会干事的裁决给出了比一些批评者更为平衡的看法。“我确实认为刘易斯稍微挤了他一下……他右侧有空间，本可以多给他一点空间，从而有可能避免接触，”欣奇克利夫说。“夏尔非得把车塞进内线吗？不，他不必。所以两人都有责任。我认为处罚过重，因为那更像是一次比赛事故。”
然而，同情在车库内消退。“内部的争斗以及责任在车队内部如何归属，当你听说在[勒克莱尔]出事前五个弯角刚被要求放轻松，然后事情就发生了，这确实会有所转变，”欣奇克利夫补充道。“我无法想象那种沮丧。”
曾担任F1车手、此次与帕尔默和欣奇克利夫一同参与解说的胡安·巴勃罗·蒙托亚支持加强纪律约束，坚称“法拉利内部必须对这类事情有更严厉的后果”。随后不久接受F1 TV采访时，勒克莱尔并未对自己的10秒罚时提出异议，他承认：“赛车之间发生碰撞仍然不可接受，再说一次，这次事件带来的一切责任我都愿意承担。”
detailEn: F1 pundit calls for real consequences at Ferrari: "I'd chuck Ollie Bearman in for a race"
James Hinchcliffe suggests Ferrari should bench a driver for Oliver Bearman for a race after their Las Vegas GP clash
Charles Leclerc, Ferrari, Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari
For Ferrari fans. The latest Scuderia Ferrari F1 news, driver updates, technical analysis and race reaction from Maranello and beyond.

After Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton collided for the second time in three races during the 2026 Las Vegas Grand Prix, the paddock debate quickly moved past who misjudged Turn 7 and onto a harder question: how can Ferrari actually stop it from happening again?

Speaking on F1 TV’s post-race show, former IndyCar driver James Hinchcliffe suggested team principal Fred Vasseur may need to reach for the ultimate deterrent - handing a race seat to Ferrari protege Oliver Bearman.
"Where do you go from here? I mean, you can't bench one of them - that's what you'd want to do," Hinchcliffe started, prompting co-analyst Jolyon Palmer to interject, "Maybe you can."

Hinchcliffe immediately ran with the idea. "I mean, I'd chuck Bearman in for a race and sit one of them out and say, 'Let's teach you guys a lesson,' like, there's some serious consequences here," he said. "But I don't know what else Fred can do, so I'm with you; I feel really bad for him."

To Hinchcliffe, what made the Lap 38 tangle so baffling was the context of a record-shattering 352-overtake contest. "This isn't Monaco. That wasn't your one shot to get by, so don't take an unnecessary risk," he noted.
Charles Leclerc, Ferrari, Lewis Hamilton, Ferrari

Even so, Hinchcliffe offered a more balanced view of the stewards' ruling than some critics. "I do think that Lewis crowded him a little bit... he had room on his right, he could have given him a bit more room and potentially avoided the contact," Hinchcliffe said. "Did Charles have to throw it up the inside? No, he didn't. So they're both to blame. I thought the penalty was harsh, 'cause it's more of a racing incident than that."

Where sympathy faded, however, was inside the garage. "The internal battle and where the blame lies within the team, it certainly shifts a little bit when you hear that five corners before [Leclerc] had just been told to take it easy, and then that happens," Hinchcliffe added. "I can't imagine the frustration."

Former F1 driver Juan Pablo Montoya, who joined Palmer and Hinchcliffe on the broadcast, backed the push for tougher discipline, insisting "there's got to be stronger consequences within Ferrari for those things". Speaking to F1 TV shortly afterwards, Leclerc did not contest his 10-second penalty, admitting, "It's still not acceptable to have a clash between cars, and again, I'll accept the blame for whatever comes with this incident."

items.titleZh: 布克斯顿：F1在美国靠文化影响力立足
items.summaryZh: 评论员威尔·布克斯顿表示，尽管F1在美国的受欢迎程度不及纳斯卡和印地赛车，但其“文化影响力”使其在美国体育版图中占据独特位置。
items.originalTitle: F1's 'cultural relevance' beats its US motorsport competition
items.summaryEn: Broadcaster Will Buxton said that although Formula 1 is less popular in the United States than NASCAR and IndyCar, its "cultural relevance" gives it a unique spot in the country's sports landscape.
detailZh: 评论员威尔·布克斯顿表示，尽管F1在美国的受欢迎程度不及纳斯卡和印地赛车，但其“文化影响力”使其在美国体育版图中占据独特位置。
布克斯顿曾在2018至2024年期间在F1TV频道担任主持人，后于2025年加入福克斯体育担任印地赛车首席评论员。
在拉斯维加斯举行的The Race x Axios“超越比赛：创新与领导力投资”活动上，布克斯顿被问及F1转投Apple TV在美国播出是否正确。
他对Axios记者萨拉·菲舍尔表示，F1“不是美国最受欢迎的赛车运动”，排在纳斯卡和印地赛车之后。
但他补充道：“一级方程式赛车拥有这两者都不具备的东西，那就是文化相关性和文化声望。”
2025年，在Apple TV于美国转播F1之前，ESPN记录到每场F1大奖赛平均有130万观众，创下历史新高——与印地赛车持平——而纳斯卡赛车每场比赛的电视平均观众为245万。
“纳斯卡赛车没有这种待遇。你走进7-Eleven，或者走进任何一家便利店……去买一罐红牛。上面印的是康纳·齐利施吗？是肖恩·范吉斯伯根吗？不，是马克斯·维斯塔潘。因为一级方程式赛车很酷。”
“一级方程式赛车具有文化相关性。这有点像《与卡戴珊一家同行》，对吧？
“所以，《与卡戴珊一家同行》的观众规模已经不如从前了。可是，维多利亚的秘密选了谁来穿那件价值5000万美元的胸衣？是凯莉·詹娜。因为她和她一家在文化上至关重要，而且至今仍留在美国民众的心里。
“而我认为，这正是F1已经做到、并且将会被研究的事情。”
巴克斯顿补充说，收视率并不是Apple TV和F1在美国所瞄准的唯一投资回报，这与自由媒体集团首席执行官德里克·张此前的观点相呼应。
现在这已经超越了那一点。它不再只是关于体育。不再只是关于人们在周日下午收看比赛。
这关乎认可度、可见度和那种文化影响力。这就是一级方程式赛车所做到的，尤其是在美国这里。这太不可思议了。
“伯尼只对下架内容感兴趣”
巴克斯顿见证了一级方程式赛车从2017年之前伯尼·埃克莱斯顿时代到随后自由媒体时代的演变，在此期间他曾为GP2系列赛、福克斯体育和NBC体育担任解说。
作为Netflix《极速求生》的年度固定节目，他表示这档常被提及的电视节目并非F1迅猛增长的唯一原因。
“事情没那么简单，因为正如斯特凡诺[多梅尼卡利，F1首席执行官]所暗示的，《极速求生》的成功与其推出时的环境背景关系密切，节目本身的作用同样如此。
“但也不能简单地说《极速求生》就是一切，因为自由媒体集团在数字领域进行了大规模推进。
“他们创建了一个此前从未存在过的YouTube频道，以及此前从未有过的Facebook页面和Twitter账号。”
巴克斯顿指出，F1对数字媒体的新做法与前F1掌门人埃克莱斯顿的做法形成了鲜明对比。
他说：“在伯尼·埃克莱斯顿执掌时期，F1对网络内容唯一的兴趣就是将其下架，而不是上传。这是事实。”
“F1曾有一个完整的部门，其唯一职责就是寻找人们发布在网上的视频和内容。”
他补充道：“但我认为《极速求生》非常重要，因为我们不再从技术角度讲述F1的故事，而是开始从个人、情感的角度来讲述。”
我认为，这种叙事方式的转变，正是这项运动能够以不同于十年前的方式打动新车迷和新生代的核心原因。
我认为，自由媒体集团接手后一级方程式赛车所做的一切，将会被后世反复研究，研究如何让一项运动不断演进，并将其从单纯的体育资产转变为一种文化现象。
detailEn: Even though Formula 1 is less popular in the United States than NASCAR and IndyCar, its "cultural relevance" gives it a unique spot in the country's sports landscape, according to broadcaster Will Buxton.
Buxton presented on the in-house F1TV channel from 2018-24 before joining Fox Sports as lead IndyCar commentator in 2025.
During The Race x Axios's Beyond the Race: Investments in Innovation and Leadership event in Las Vegas, Buxton was asked if F1's move to Apple TV in the US was the correct one.
He replied to Axios Correspondent Sara Fischer that F1 is "not the most popular form of motorsport in America" as it sits behind NASCAR and IndyCar.
But he added: "What Formula 1 has is something that neither of those has, which is cultural relevance and cultural cachet."
In 2025, before Apple TV broadcasted F1 in the US, ESPN recorded an all-time-high of 1.3m viewers per F1 grand prix - on par with IndyCar - while NASCAR averaged 2.45m viewers per race on TV.
Buxton reflected on F1's presence on advertising screens in New York City's Times Square in 2026.

"NASCAR doesn't have that. You go into a 7-Eleven, or you go into any convenience store...to buy a can of Red Bull. Is Connor Zilisch on it? Is Shane van Gisbergen on it? No, it's Max Verstappen. Because Formula 1 is cool.
"Formula 1 has cultural relevance. It’s a bit like Keeping Up with the Kardashians, right?

"So, Keeping Up with the Kardashians does not have the audience that it once did. And yet, who did Victoria's Secret pick to wear the $50million bra? It was Kylie [Jenner]. Because she and her family are culturally vital and still are in the American population's mindset.
"And I think that's what Formula 1 has done that will be studied."
Buxton added that viewership is not the only return on investment that Apple TV and F1 will be targeting in the US, reflecting a previous sentiment of Liberty Media CEO Derek Chang.
"It's bigger than that now. It's not just about sport. It's not just about people tuning in on a Sunday afternoon to the race.
"It's about recognition and visibility and that cultural cachet. That is what Formula 1 has done, particularly here in America. That is so incredible."
'Bernie was only interested in taking content down'
Buxton has witnessed F1's evolution from the pre-2017 Bernie Ecclestone era to the following Liberty Media one, having commentated for the GP2 Series, Fox Sports, and NBC Sports over that change.
As an annual fixture of Netflix's Drive to Survive, he said that the oft-cited TV show is not the only reason for F1's momentous growth.

"It's not that simple because as Stefano [Domenicali, F1 CEO] intimated, the success of Drive to Survive had as much to do with the circumstances around when it launched as it did the programme itself.
"But it's also not as simple as to say Drive to Survive was everything because Liberty had made a massive push into the digital domain.
"They created a YouTube channel where one never existed and a Facebook page and a Twitter account where those things never existed."
Buxton noted a stark contrast between F1's new approach to digital media and that of ex-F1 supremo Ecclestone.
"The only interest that Formula 1 under Bernie Ecclestone had with online content was taking it down, not putting it up," he said. "That's true.
"There was a whole department in Formula 1 whose sole job it was to find videos and content that people had put online."

He added: "But Drive to Survive I think was really important because we stopped telling the story of Formula 1 from a technical perspective and started telling it from a personal, emotional perspective.
"And that shift in storytelling I think has laid at the heart of why the sport speaks to new fans and a new generation in a way that it perhaps didn't do 10 years ago.

"I think what Formula 1 has done since Liberty Media took over, I think it will be studied for generations to come as to how you evolve a sport and turn it from being simply a sporting property into being a cultural phenomenon."

items.summaryEn: Juan Pablo Montoya explained how Red Bull outsmarted Mercedes with its deployment strategy at the Las Vegas Grand Prix. Antonelli topped qualifying but a five-place engine penalty dropped him to sixth, and after 35 lead changes Red Bull took the win.
detailZh: 胡安·巴勃罗·蒙托亚解释了红牛如何在F1拉斯维加斯大奖赛中智胜梅赛德斯。
胡安·巴勃罗·蒙托亚解释了红牛的能量部署陷阱如何在拉斯维加斯这场出现352次超车的激战中智胜梅赛德斯。
致红牛车迷。关注红牛车队，获取来自米尔顿凯恩斯的F1新闻、车手动态、技术洞察与比赛分析。
梅赛德斯为拉斯维加斯大道带来了最快的单圈套件——新加冕的2026年世界冠军基米·安东内利在排位赛中排名第一，但五位的引擎罚退使他降至第六，而乔治·拉塞尔与杆位得主马克斯·维斯塔潘同排发车。
然而在50圈混乱的比赛和35次领先变化之后，红牛捧起了奖杯，而两辆银箭赛车均未登上领奖台。
七届大奖赛冠军胡安·巴勃罗·蒙托亚在F1电视台赛后转播中指出了红牛智胜对手的原因。
“不仅是马克斯，红牛的战略也非常出色，”蒙托亚说。“梅赛德斯采用了追求最快圈速的策略，他们认为这是在正常比赛中绕行此地的最快方式。我不认为他们预料到我们会每圈都互相超越。”
安德烈亚·基米·安东内利，梅赛德斯，马克斯·维斯塔潘，红牛车队
在这场以352次超车打破一级方程式赛车超车纪录的比赛中，如果在计时线前赛车耗尽电能，那么直道上的原始速度就几乎毫无意义。蒙托亚解释道：“红牛总会在直道上牺牲一点速度，他总会被超越，但马克斯总能在终点线前追回来。”
排位赛的数据凸显了这一冒险策略：维斯塔潘在测速点仅排第18位，他把电能留到了最后一个弯道的出弯处，一直冲向终点。蒙托亚在为西班牙语电视台解说比赛时看到这一模式反复出现，他知道梅赛德斯没有简单的答案。“他们唯一能击败马克斯的办法，就是如果能有两辆车插在中间，也就是如果有两个人能在长直道上超越他，那么他们才有机会。如果只有一辆车，马克斯就会赢。而他们做得超出了预期。”
在比赛工程师汤姆·哈特的墙边指导下——哈特在替代詹皮耶罗·兰比亚塞时庆祝了自己的首场胜利——维斯塔潘确认他不断与红牛沟通，以保护终点线前的冲刺。
维斯塔潘对F1电视台说：“只是人们在改变电能部署，我想确保车队专注于此，确保我们在终点线前有尽可能最好的电能部署，当然不会在其他地方牺牲太多，但要确保如果终点线前有战斗，我们处于正确的电能部署状态。”
蒙托亚仍然特别指出拉塞尔是“唯一一个稍微摸清了维斯塔潘套路的人”，并指出他能量管理得足够好，即便两次跑宽，仍能在进入1号弯时领先。拉塞尔后来承认，在直道上最多赚到1.3秒让他在中段暴露无遗——而在第48圈，他在脏线上攻击安东内利时于5号弯锁死，滑入护栏，最终第九名完赛。
片刻之后，安东内利在背直道上收油再给油，试图管理身后维斯塔潘的位置，结果完全耗尽电池，从第二跌至第四，落在两辆迈凯伦之后——让托托·沃尔夫计划中的最后400米冲刺未能用上。
维斯塔潘2026年的第四个第一名——也是生涯第75个——使他的积分升至304分，在车手积分榜上落后安东内利（402分）排名第二，领先刘易斯·汉密尔顿（267分）37分，领先拉塞尔（264分）40分。梅赛德斯或许把最快单圈赛车带到了内华达，但红牛把这场棋局读得透彻得多。
detailEn: Juan Pablo Montoya explains how Red Bull outsmarted Mercedes at F1 Las Vegas GP
Juan Pablo Montoya explains how Red Bull's deployment trap outsmarted Mercedes in Las Vegas's 352-overtake thriller
For Red Bull fans. Keeping watch on Red Bull Racing, with F1 news, driver updates, technical insight and race analysis from Milton Keynes.

Mercedes brought the fastest single-lap package to the Las Vegas Strip - newly crowned 2026 world champion Kimi Antonelli topped qualifying before a five-place engine penalty dropped him to sixth, while George Russell lined up alongside polesitter Max Verstappen.
Yet after 50 chaotic laps and 35 lead changes, Red Bull collected the trophy while neither Silver Arrow reached the podium.
Speaking on F1 TV’s post-race broadcast, seven-time grand prix winner Juan Pablo Montoya pinpointed why Red Bull outfoxed its rival.

"Not only Max, but Red Bull's strategy was so good," Montoya said. "Mercedes went with the strategy for the fastest lap and what they thought would be the fastest way around here for a normal race. I don't think they were expecting that we're going to be passing each other every lap."
Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes, Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing

In a contest that shattered Formula 1’s overtaking record with 352 passes, raw velocity down the Strip counted for little if a car ran dry before the timing beam. "Red Bull would always sacrifice a little bit on the Strip, and he could always get passed, but Max always came back at the line," Montoya explained.

Qualifying numbers underscored that gamble: Verstappen ranked just 18th through the speed trap, saving electrical punch for the exit of the final corner toward the flag. Watching the pattern repeat while calling the race for Spanish-language television, Montoya knew Mercedes had no simple answer. "The only way they could beat Max, if they could put two cars in between, is if two people could pass him in the long straight, then they would have had a shot. If it was one car, Max was going to win. And they outdid themselves."

Guided on the pitwall by race engineer Tom Hart - who celebrated his maiden victory substituting for Gianpiero Lambiase - Verstappen confirmed he constantly checked with Red Bull to protect that finish-line kick.

"It's just people changing their deployment, and I wanted to make sure that the team was on it, that we had the best possible deployment to the line without, of course, compromising too much other places, but to make sure that if there was a fight to the line that we were on the right deployment," Verstappen told F1 TV.

Montoya still singled out Russell as "the only guy that figured out a little bit of Max," noting he managed energy well enough to lead into Turn 1 even after running wide twice. Russell later admitted gaining up to 1.3 seconds down the Strip left him exposed in the middle sector—and on Lap 48, he locked up on the dirty line attacking Antonelli at Turn 5, sliding into the barrier and finishing ninth.

Moments later, Antonelli lifted and reapplied throttle down the back straight trying to manage position behind Verstappen, completely draining his battery and tumbling from second to fourth behind both McLarens - leaving Toto Wolff’s planned final-400-metre push unused.

Verstappen’s fourth P1 of 2026 - and 75th overall - lifted him to 304 points, moving 37 clear of Lewis Hamilton (267) and 40 ahead of Russell (264) for second in the drivers’ championship behind Antonelli (402). Mercedes may have brought the quickest one-lap car to Nevada, but Red Bull read the chess match far better.

detailZh: 哈贾尔在拉斯维加斯无线电中表达不满——红牛无线电里究竟发生了什么
哈贾尔在拉斯维加斯比赛中主张采用类似自行车赛的战术，红牛对其进步表示认可
哈贾尔从第四位发车参加F1拉斯维加斯大奖赛，到第四圈时他已升至第二位，紧随红牛队友维斯塔潘。
鉴于这场比赛已演变成只能被形容为类似场地自行车赛那样的尾流争夺战，哈贾尔迟早会尝试争夺领先位置，这几乎是不可避免的。
但他的比赛工程师理查德·伍德很快就发出了提醒。伍德解释说，首要任务是避免车队整体损失时间。红牛需要拉开与乔治·拉塞尔的差距，而不是把宝贵的时间浪费在内斗上。而哈贾尔——当然并不缺乏自信，但归根结底是红牛忠诚的团队成员——照办了。
最终，他在通往14号弯的长直道上再次与维斯塔潘并排。但这位荷兰人无意不战而降让出领先位置。“他能不能别再防守了？不然我只会损失时间，”哈贾尔在无线电中抱怨道。然而伍德坚持他们此前已经商定的计划：“车队要求是防守乔治，否则我们会来回拉锯。”
当时，拉塞尔是前方红牛快车最接近的追赶者，三人愉快地交换着位置。有一次，拉塞尔甚至同时超越了两位红牛车手，结果两三个弯后又发现自己回到了第三位。在拉斯维加斯，尾流和能量管理是强大的武器。事实上，比纯粹的速度更强大。
哈贾尔的无线电信息清楚地表明，从车队角度来看，他更希望看到类似自行车运动中轮转领骑的配合，而非传统的编队行驶：一组车手通过不断轮换领骑来协同工作，让每个成员都能从尾流中受益，使整个团队比单个车手独自骑行更快。
但红牛显然对这场比赛的特殊态势有些措手不及，似乎对哈贾尔的提议并不特别感兴趣。为了拉开与拉塞尔的差距而共享领先位置的想法，甚至没有与维斯塔潘讨论过。至少，在这位荷兰车手的官方车载无线电频道中，听不到相应的询问。
马克斯·维斯塔潘，红牛车队，伊萨克·哈贾尔，红牛车队
最终，哈贾尔受够了。“不，你看，我现在就给你举个例子。看看接下来会发生什么，”他在无线电中说。而恰恰就在那一刻，他没有刻意提前松油门以避免在14号弯攻击维斯塔潘，而是继续踩住油门。结果相当壮观。哈贾尔以数米的优势超过队友，取得领先。随后，他始终以团队为重，又放慢速度，让维斯塔潘在入弯前重新夺回第一的位置。
但他已经表明了自己的观点。“我做不到。在直道上，差距太大了。这比你想象的更难。我没有撒谎。”
哈贾尔认为，如果允许他超越维斯塔潘，两辆红牛赛车整体上会更快，结果维斯塔潘在下一圈就夺回了位置。与其不必要地互相拖慢，他们本可以利用巨大的尾流优势来维持集体的速度。这是一个简单直接的提议：轮流领跑，从彼此的尾流中获益，并尽可能快地向前推进。
这一切都发生在第八圈。几乎就像是比赛本身决心要证明哈贾尔的论点正确一样，仅仅一圈之后，红牛的一二名阵型就消失了。车队未能甩开拉塞尔。
赛后有人问，红牛坚持不惜一切代价保护维斯塔潘的领先地位，是否实际上损害了自己的机会，车队领队洛朗·梅基斯承认哈贾尔提出了一个合理的观点。
“说得有道理，”梅基斯承认。“我想首先要说的是，尽管我们都知道这是一条能量匮乏的赛道，我们都预计比赛中会有很多博弈，尽管我们昨天看到了比预期大得多的尾流效应，我想我们没有人会在比赛前想到，我们会在50圈里每圈有两次超车。”换句话说，就连红牛也低估了尾流效应会变得多么极端。
马克斯·维斯塔潘，红牛车队，伊萨克·哈贾尔，红牛车队
"那么我为什么这么说呢？因为我确实认为，在最初几圈里，我们都必须适应这场比赛的新现实。"这解释了为什么红牛的战略师们不愿采纳哈贾尔的做法。"而且我们并不觉得每圈交换赛车位置会是坚持到终点最快的方式。我们永远不会知道答案。我们觉得，如果两辆车都能互相帮助防守身后的位置，那肯定更好。"
经过几个小时的回顾之后，梅基斯对那个判断已不像比赛中那样确定了。毕竟，没有人能肯定地说，哈贾尔的轮换领先策略是否本可以让两辆红牛摆脱拉塞尔。
最终，这个问题自行解决了——哈贾尔的前翼突然断裂，实际上终结了这位22岁车手的胜利希望。难怪赛后当被问及车队无线电讨论的话题时，他的回应有些恼火："没有误解。我不是想制造混乱。只是动动脑子而已。"
无论有意与否，这确实可以被解读为对红牛维修区墙的一次言语暗讽。哈贾尔解释了他采取这种策略背后的思路：“我试图做的，因为我懂赛车，就是你需要尽可能快地跑。这无所谓。你只需要往前冲，超车，被反超回来，再超车。你就得一直这样跑。因为如果我压着速度，那么后面的人、后面的车就会直接超过我，因为速度差有40公里/小时。”
这位法国车手确信红牛只是低估了尾流的非凡影响力：“我觉得他们只是没意识到尾流博弈有多重要。不是说我只要跟在后面就行，如果那样做，乔治就会过去。要么我拼一把，我们俩都全速跑，超来超去。那才是最快的比赛。如果你让我跟在后面、直接放弃位置，那对我来说行不通。”
然而，尽管有这些沮丧情绪，哈贾尔在拉斯维加斯实际上可能大大提升了自己在红牛内部的地位。首先，他再次证明了自己是长期以来第一位至少能在比赛的某些阶段接近维斯塔潘表现水平的队友。其次，任何关于他可能只是在自私行事、利用巧妙的无线电信息为自己越过维斯塔潘创造条件的残留怀疑，现在都应该被消除了。
马克斯·维斯塔潘，红牛车队，伊萨克·哈贾尔，红牛车队
哈贾尔的处理方式表明，他考虑的是车队的整体表现，而不仅仅是自己的位置。这种行为能够建立信任，而梅基斯恰恰对此赞不绝口：“说实话，我认为他做得非常、非常好。
“他凭实力出现在那里，他之所以在那里是因为他有速度，他之所以在那里是因为他非常清楚地理解防守和进攻的动作，这对我们来说是最好的情况。而且当我们要求他把缠斗留到后面、集中精力不被身后的人追上也时，他也理解得很好。”
对梅基斯来说，这次事件进一步证明了哈贾尔在整个赛季中的成长：“今年我们已经说过很多次了，他一场比一场进步。这也是我们今天又一次看到的。他在发车格上排第四，在赛道上跑到过第一、第二。上周末，我们拿到了第二、第三，而且上周末我们不得不交换了赛车。所以这是好消息。”
除了绝对速度之外，这位红牛车队领队还强调了哈贾尔取得重大进步的另一领域：情绪控制。“伊萨克是一个非常聪明的人，对我们这些非车手来说，很难评估车手在车内必须应对的情绪管理问题，”他说。
“他认识到了这一点，他非常清楚，更好地管理这些情绪能让他在车内赢得圈速，也能在车外通过与工程师的沟通质量赢得圈速。正如你指出的，他在过去两三场比赛中取得了非常非常大的进步。我们预计未来还有更大的潜力。”
“因此，他与工程团队的交流越来越好，当他能够控制住情绪时，他的执行也更强。我们对他取得的进步非常满意。”
detailEn: Isack Hadjar frustrated – What really happened on Red Bull's team radio in Las Vegas
Hadjar advocated for cycling-like tactics in the Las Vegas race, and Red Bull is impressed with his progress
Isack Hadjar started Formula 1’s Las Vegas Grand Prix from fourth on the grid, and by lap four he had already found himself running second, right behind Red Bull team-mate Max Verstappen.

And given that the grand prix had turned into what can only be described as a slipstreaming battle of the kind normally associated with track cycling, it was almost inevitable that Hadjar would sooner or later have a go at taking the lead.

But a reminder from his race engineer Richard Wood was not long in coming. The priority, Wood explained, was to avoid losing time as a team. Red Bull needed to build a gap to George Russell, rather than waste precious seconds fighting among themselves. And Hadjar, certainly no stranger to self-confidence but ultimately a loyal Red Bull team player, complied.

Eventually, he found himself alongside Verstappen again on the long straight towards Turn 14. But the Dutchman had no intention of surrendering the lead without a fight. "Can he stop defending? Otherwise I just gotta lose time," Hadjar complained over the radio. Wood, however, stuck to the plan they had already agreed upon: "Team request is to defend against George, otherwise we will be yo-yoing."

At that point, Russell was the closest pursuer of the Red Bull Express at the front, with the trio merrily swapping positions. On one occasion, Russell even managed to overtake both Red Bulls simultaneously, only to find himself back in third place two or three corners later. In Las Vegas, slipstreaming and energy management were powerful weapons. More powerful, in fact, than outright speed.

Hadjar's radio messages made it clear that, from a team perspective, he would have preferred something resembling a rotating paceline in cycling over conventional formation driving: a group of riders works together by constantly rotating the lead, allowing each member to benefit from the slipstream and enabling the group as a whole to travel faster than an individual rider could manage alone.

But Red Bull, apparently caught somewhat off guard by the peculiar dynamics of the race, did not seem particularly interested in Hadjar's proposal. The idea of sharing the lead in order to open up a gap to Russell was not even discussed with Verstappen. At least, there is no corresponding question to be heard on the Dutchman's official onboard radio feed.
Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing, Isack Hadjar, Red Bull Racing

Eventually, Hadjar had had enough. "No, look, I'm gonna give you an example right now. Look at what's gonna happen," he radioed. And at precisely that moment, rather than deliberately lifting off the throttle early to avoid attacking Verstappen into Turn 14, he kept his foot down. The result was quite spectacular. Hadjar sailed past his team-mate by several metres and into the lead. Then, ever the team player, he backed off again and allowed Verstappen to reclaim first place before the corner.
But he had made his point. "I can't. On the straight, there's too big of a difference. It's harder than you think. I'm not lying."

Hadjar argued that the two Red Bulls would be faster overall if he were allowed to overtake Verstappen, only for Verstappen to retake the position on the following lap. Rather than unnecessarily slowing one another down, they could use the enormous slipstream advantage to maintain their collective pace. It was a straightforward proposition: take turns leading, benefit from each other's slipstream, and keep moving forward as quickly as possible.

All of this happened on lap eight. And almost as if the race itself were determined to vindicate Hadjar's argument, Red Bull's 1-2 formation was gone just one lap later. The team had failed to shake off Russell.

Asked afterwards whether Red Bull might actually have compromised its own chances by insisting on protecting Verstappen's lead at all costs, team principal Laurent Mekies acknowledged that Hadjar had made a legitimate point.

"Fair points," Mekies admitted. "I think the first thing to say is that as much as we all knew it was an energy-poor track and we were all expecting a lot of gaming in the race, as much as we saw yesterday the much bigger than expected slipstream effect, I think none of us were going to the race thinking that we'll have two overtaking per lap for 50 laps." In other words, even Red Bull had underestimated just how extreme the slipstreaming effect would prove to be.
Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing, Isack Hadjar, Red Bull Racing

"So why am I saying that? Because I truly think that in the first few laps we all had to adapt on what is the new reality for this race." That explains why Red Bull's strategists were reluctant to embrace Hadjar's approach. "And we didn't feel that swapping the car every lap would be the fastest way to go to the end. We will never know the answer. And we felt it was certainly better if both cars could help each other defend on the positions behind."

With the benefit of a few hours' hindsight, Mekies was no longer quite as certain about that judgement as he had been during the race. After all, nobody could say for sure whether Hadjar's rotating-lead strategy might have enabled the two Red Bulls to escape from Russell.

Eventually, the issue resolved itself when Hadjar's front wing suddenly broke, effectively ending the 22-year-old's victory hopes. Little wonder, then, that his response was somewhat irritated when the subject of the team radio discussion was raised after the race: "There was no misunderstanding. I wasn't trying to create a mess. It's just using my brain."

Whether intentionally or otherwise, that could certainly be interpreted as a verbal dig at the Red Bull pitwall. Hadjar explained the thinking behind his approach: "What I'm trying to do, because I understand racing, is you need to go as fast as possible. It doesn't matter. You need to just go, overtake, get overtaken back, overtake. You just need to keep going. Because if I hold back, then the guy behind and the car behind is just going to overtake me because there's 40km/h difference."

The Frenchman was convinced that Red Bull had simply underestimated the extraordinary influence of the slipstream: "I think they just didn't realise how big the tow games were. It's not like I can just sit behind and if I do that then George goes through. It's either I go for it and we both go flat out, passing, re-passing. That was the fastest race. If you tell me to sit behind and just give up the position then it's not going to work for me."

For all his frustration, however, Hadjar may actually have done his standing within Red Bull a great deal of good in Las Vegas. First, he once again demonstrated that he is the first team-mate in a long time capable of operating, at least for certain stretches of a race, in something approaching Verstappen's performance territory. And second, any lingering suspicions that he might simply be acting selfishly, using clever radio messages to manoeuvre himself past Verstappen, should now have been put to rest.
Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing, Isack Hadjar, Red Bull Racing

Hadjar’s approach demonstrated that he was thinking about the team's overall performance rather than merely his own position. This sort of behaviour builds trust, And Mekies was full of praise for precisely that: "I think he did very, very good, honestly.

"He was there on merit, he was there because he had the pace, he was there because he was understanding very well the defensive, offensive manoeuvres, and that's the best situation possible for us. And he also understood well when we asked him to keep the battles for later and to concentrate on not getting caught by the guys behind."

For Mekies, the incident was further evidence of Hadjar's development over the course of the season: "We have been saying so many times this year, he's improving race after race. That's also what we see another time today. He was P4 on the grid, P1, P2 on the road. Last weekend, we did P2, P3, and we had to swap the cars last weekend. So it's good news."

Beyond his outright pace, the Red Bull team principal highlighted another area in which Hadjar has been making substantial progress: emotional control. "Isack is a very intelligent individual, and it's very difficult for us non-drivers to assess what drivers have to deal with in terms of management of their emotions when they are in the car," he said.

"And he recognised that, he knows very well that managing these emotions better gives him lap time in the car and lap time outside of the car in terms of the quality of the communication with his engineers. And as you pointed out, he made very, very big steps in the last two, three races. And we see even more potential moving forward."
"So he's exchanging better and better with his engineering crew, and he's executing stronger when he's able to keep his emotions under control. And we are very happy with the progress he's making."

detailZh: 马克斯·维斯塔潘调侃说，他上一次赢下像F1拉斯维加斯大奖赛这样的比赛还是在玩《马里奥赛车》的时候。

四届F1世界冠军马克斯·维斯塔潘表示，他上一次赢下像拉斯维加斯大奖赛这样的比赛还是在玩《马里奥赛车》的时候。
这位红牛车手将杆位转化为他的第75场大奖赛胜利，也是他在拉斯维加斯的第三场胜利，这场比赛共有352次超车和35次领先变化。
在赛后新闻发布会上被问及他上一次赢得这样的比赛是什么时候时，这位荷兰人起初不愿回答：“我大概不该说。我大概真的不该说。我记得我玩马里奥赛车时赢过一场这样的比赛。”
“有时候你掉到后面，你会获得尾流，然后就像有一种追赶效果，你知道吗？每次你掉到后面，你都会跑得更快。所以那是我上一次感受到类似这样的东西，”他说。
这位红牛车手多次被超越失去领先位置，主要是被梅赛德斯的乔治·拉塞尔超越，但他每次都反击回来。虽然他成功重新夺回领先，但他无法扩大优势并甩开身后的车群。
“这纯粹是尾流配合能量释放的效果。当然，当你在1秒以内时，你还有超车模式，而在这里那非常强大。所以，是的，你无法拉开差距。”
当被问及是否享受在拉斯维加斯街道上的比赛时，维斯塔潘在车手和观众之间划了一条界线。
“当我从赛车手的心来看待它时，不。当你把它当作一场表演、一场奇观来看时，是的。我享受了我的反超和一切，但我更愿意用我的赛车心来看待它。”
这场比赛几乎没有让他的脉搏加快。“甚至我的心率，我一点也不紧张，因为，我不知道，在那里感觉就像是在巡航，只是在正确的时候尝试按下电池或防守。但为了表演，当你从外面看它时，大概是的，你喜欢它。”
维斯塔潘目前在车手积分榜上排名第二。梅赛德斯的基米·安东内利在墨西哥大奖赛上锁定了年度冠军，但第二名之争将延续到即将到来的卡塔尔大奖赛。维斯塔潘领先排名第三的刘易斯·汉密尔顿37分。乔治·拉塞尔和兰多·诺里斯分列第四和第五，两人同为264分。
detailEn: Max Verstappen jokes last time he won a race like F1 Las Vegas GP it was "Mario Kart"
The Red Bull driver compared the slipstream battles on the Las Vegas Strip to Nintendo's racing game
For Red Bull fans. Keeping watch on Red Bull Racing, with F1 news, driver updates, technical insight and race analysis from Milton Keynes.
Four-time Formula 1 champion Max Verstappen says the last time he won a race like the Las Vegas Grand Prix was when he was playing Mario Kart.
The Red Bull driver converted pole position into his 75th grand prix win, and his third in Las Vegas, in a race that featured 352 overtakes and 35 lead changes.

Asked during the post-race press conference when he had last won a race like it, the Dutchman was reluctant to answer at first: "I probably shouldn't say it. I probably should not. I remember winning one like this when I was playing Mario Kart.
"Sometimes you drop back and you get drafts, and there's like a catch-up, you know? Always when you're dropping back, you go faster. So that's the last time that I felt something like this," he said.

The Red Bull driver was passed for the lead time and again, mostly by Mercedes' George Russell, and hit back every time. While he managed to retake the lead, he was not able to extend his advantage and break away from the pack behind him.

"It was just the tow combination with the deployment. Of course, when you are within a second, you have the overtake mode as well, and around here that is powerful. So, yeah, you could not pull away."
Asked whether he had enjoyed the race around the streets of Las Vegas, Verstappen drew a line between the driver and the spectator.
"When I look at it from my racer heart, no. When you look at it as a show, spectacle, yes. I've enjoyed my repassing and everything, but I prefer to look at it with my racing heart."

The race barely raised his pulse. "Even my heart rate, I was not nervous at all because, I don't know, it just felt kind of cruising out there, just trying to press the battery whenever it was correct or defend. But for the show, when you look at it from the outside, probably yes, you like it."

Verstappen currently sits second in the drivers' standings. Mercedes' Kimi Antonelli claimed the title at the Mexican Grand Prix but the fight for second will continue into the upcoming Qatar Grand Prix. Verstappen has a 37-point lead over Lewis Hamilton, who sits third. George Russell and Lando Norris are fourth and fifth, respectively, both on 264 points.

detailZh: 洛朗·梅基斯：保持情绪稳定正为伊萨克·哈贾尔带来“圈速”
洛朗·梅基斯表示，伊萨克·哈贾尔在拉斯维加斯一鸣惊人之后，保持情绪稳定正在释放“圈速”潜力
致红牛车迷。关注红牛车队，获取来自米尔顿凯恩斯的F1新闻、车手动态、技术洞察与赛事分析。
伊萨克·哈贾尔在2026年拉斯维加斯大奖赛上空手而归——第26圈前翼故障，加上赛后10秒安全车处罚，使他跌至第15名——然而红牛车队领队洛朗·梅基斯在拉斯维加斯大道上看到了远为令人鼓舞的东西。
这位22岁的车手在排位赛中取得第四名，并在第9圈与最终夺冠的马克斯·维斯塔潘形成早期的一二名领跑时短暂领先，赢得了梅基斯的盛赞——梅基斯认为哈贾尔日益增强的情绪稳定性如今正直接转化为速度。
在赛后媒体采访中被问及哈贾尔在周四宣称在最后三站追逐胜利“没什么可失去的”之后所展现出的无畏态度时，梅基斯同时称赞了他的速度和战术纪律。
“说实话，他做得非常非常好，”梅基斯说。“他靠实力站在那里；他站在那里是因为他有速度；他站在那里是因为他非常理解防守和进攻的动作，这对我们来说是最好的情况。他也很好地理解了当我们要求他把战斗留到后面、专注于不被身后的人追上的时候。”
梅基斯指出连续两个突破性的周末——包括两周前的圣保罗大奖赛，哈贾尔在那里让位于强势追赶的维斯塔潘获得第二名，随后又拿下他2026年的第三个领奖台——作为稳步成长的证明。“他在发车格上是第四名，在赛道上是一、二名，”梅基斯指出。“上周末，我们取得了第二、第三名，而且上周末我们不得不交换了赛车。所以这是好消息。”
这份冷静标志着这位车手的明显转变——在他随高级车队征战的首个赛季早些时候，他火爆的脾气曾引起关注：从六月摩纳哥站登上领奖台过程中麻烦不断的无线电交锋，到上个月在奥斯汀练习赛中与亚历克斯·阿尔本令人沮丧的碰撞后被国际汽联警告。据梅基斯所说，保持更冷静的头脑正在维修区墙两侧释放出性能。
“伊萨克非常聪明，对我们这些非车手的人来说，很难评估车手在车内必须应对的情绪管理问题，”梅基斯解释道。
马克斯·维斯塔潘，红牛车队，伊萨克·哈贾尔，红牛车队
“他认识到了这一点，他非常清楚，更好地管理这些情绪能让他在车内获得圈速，也能在车外通过与工程师沟通的质量获得圈速。
正如你所指出的，他在过去两三场比赛中取得了非常非常大的进步。而且我们看到未来还有更多潜力。因此，他与工程团队之间的交流越来越好。当他能够控制住自己的情绪时，他的执行也更强了。
红牛方面则另行承认，就尾翼突然断裂一事应向哈贾尔道歉——而赛会干事因他在安全车后减速约100公里/小时、为维斯塔潘制造双车进站间隔而对他处以10秒罚时——拉斯维加斯站对他第八名、122分的积分几乎没有帮助。
尽管如此，在进入卡塔尔站和阿布扎比站之际，红牛正以440分对431分、领先迈凯伦9分捍卫车队积分榜第三的位置，哈贾尔更犀利的执行可能成为决定性因素。
detailEn: Laurent Mekies: Keeping his emotions in check is giving Isack Hadjar “lap time”
Laurent Mekies says Isack Hadjar keeping his emotions in check is unlocking "lap time" after a breakout Las Vegas run
For Red Bull fans. Keeping watch on Red Bull Racing, with F1 news, driver updates, technical insight and race analysis from Milton Keynes.

Isack Hadjar left the 2026 Las Vegas Grand Prix empty-handed after a Lap 26 front wing failure and a post-race 10-second safety car penalty relegated him to 15th, yet Red Bull team principal Laurent Mekies saw something far more encouraging on the Strip.

Having qualified fourth and briefly led on Lap 9 during an early one–two run alongside eventual winner Max Verstappen, the 22-year-old earned glowing praise from Mekies - who believes Hadjar’s growing emotional composure is now translating directly into speed.

Asked in his post-race media session about the fearless approach Hadjar showed after declaring on Thursday he had "nothing to lose" in chasing a win across the final three rounds, Mekies credited both his pace and tactical discipline.

"He did very, very good, honestly," Mekies said. "He was there on merit; he was there because he had the pace; he was there because he was understanding very well the defensive, offensive manoeuvres, and that’s the best situation possible for us. And he also understood well when we asked him to keep the battles for later and to concentrate on not getting caught by the guys behind."

Mekies pointed to consecutive breakthrough weekends - including the Sao Paulo Grand Prix two weeks earlier, where Hadjar yielded second to a charging Verstappen before securing his third podium of 2026 - as proof of steady growth. "He was P4 on the grid, P1, P2 on the road," Mekies noted. "Last weekend, we did P2, P3, and we had to swap the cars last weekend. So it’s good news."

That calm marks a noticeable shift for a driver whose fiery temperament drew attention earlier in his first season with the senior team - from heated radio exchanges during a troubled Monaco podium run in June to an FIA warning in Austin last month after a frustrating clash with Alex Albon in practice. According to Mekies, keeping a cooler head is unlocking performance on both sides of the pitwall.

"Isack is a very intelligent individual, and it’s very difficult for us non-drivers to assess what drivers have to deal with in terms of management of their emotions when they are in the car," Mekies explained.
Max Verstappen, Red Bull Racing, Isack Hadjar, Red Bull Racing

"He recognised that, he knows very well that managing these emotions better gives him lap time in the car and lap time outside of the car in terms of the quality of the communication with his engineers.

"And as you pointed out, he made very, very big steps in the last two, three races. And we see even more potential moving forward. So he’s exchanging better and better with his engineering crew. And he’s executing stronger when he’s able to keep his emotions under control."

With Red Bull separately admitting it owed Hadjar an apology over the sudden wing collapse - while stewards handed him a 10-second penalty for slowing roughly 100 km/h behind the safety car to create a double-stack gap for Verstappen - Las Vegas did little for his eighth-place tally of 122 points.
Still, with Red Bull defending a nine-point edge over McLaren for third in the constructors’ standings (440 to 431) entering Qatar and Abu Dhabi, Hadjar’s sharper execution could prove decisive.
